content.title: Arkansas earns first SEC tournament title since 2000 with 86-75 win over Vanderbilt
content.text: Darius Acuff Jr. continued his spectacular freshman season, scoring 30 points with 11 assists to lead Arkansas to an 86-75 win over Vanderbilt in the SEC championship game on Sunday in Nashville.Acuff became the first player in SEC tournament history with 30 or more points and 10-plus assists.Advertisement[Enter Yahoo Fantasy Bracket Mayhem now for your shot at $50K]Trevon Brazile was the closer for the Razorbacks, hitting two consecutive 3-pointers for an 80-72 lead. With the Commodores needing a basket to prevent Arkansas from pulling away, Brazile also blocked a shot by Jalen Washington. That led to a breakaway layup for Malique Ewin and a 10-point lead.The Razorbacks won their first conference tournament title since 2000, and avoided a seventh runner-up finish since joining the SEC for the 1991-92 season.Arkansas shot 63% (15-of-24) from 3-point range, which was a major factor in its win. Acuff went 5-for-8 from behind the arc, while Brazile swished four of his five attempts. D.J. Wagner also went 3-for-3, while Billy Richmond III hit two of his four 3-pointers.AdvertisementBrazile finished with 16 points, 9 rebounds, 2 steals and 2 blocks, while Richmond scored 18 with 5 boards and 3 assists. Wagner added 11 points off the bench.Vanderbilt almost matched that long-range accuracy, knocking down 10-of-24 3-point attempts. Tyler Nickel shot 5-of-7 on his 3-point tries and Duke Miles shot 3-for-6. Nickel scored 19 points with 9 rebounds for the Commodores, while Miles also scored 19 with 9 assists.After a six-point burst gave Vanderbilt a 55-49 lead, Arkansas answered with an 11-0 run fueled by two 3-pointers from Wagner and another by Acuff to go back on top.The Commodores had an opportunity to tie the score with just over four minutes remaining, but Tyler Tanner missed a layup. Acuff followed by knocking down a midrange jumper for a 74-70 lead.AdvertisementVanderbilt is projected to be a No. 4 seed when the NCAA tournament bracket is announced later on Sunday. The Commodores started off the season red-hot with a 16-0 record, but losses started to pile up during a midseason lull. No matter; they’re back to their winning ways as we head into March Madness.Arkansas winning the conference title in head coach John Calipari’s second season (adding to the six he won with Kentucky) was a surprising development. The regular season was all about Florida and whether Todd Golden’s team will run it back with another national title.The Gators looked strong entering the SEC tournament only to get routed by Vanderbilt in the semifinals. Now, it’s up to the NCAA tournament selection committee to decide whether to award them a No. 1 seed.AdvertisementHere is how the SEC tournament bracket played out.
